numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Calling numpy.resize with an unsigned integer size (np.uint32(1) or np.uint64(1)) emits 'RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative' from the line repeats = -(-new_size // a.size). The uint32 call then raises SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned NULL without setting an exception, and the uint64 call raises OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer. The negation of an unsigned int underflows and creates a large positive repeats value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.resize(np.array([[23, 95], [66, 37]]), np.uint32(1)) should return [23], as the signed np.int32(1) case does.
trigger_conditions: new_shape/size argument is an unsigned integer NumPy scalar such as np.uint32 or np.uint64
a.size is nonzero and new_size is greater than zero so the ceil-division path is taken

input_output_examples.buggy_output: SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned NULL without setting an exception (preceded by RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative)
OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer

numerical_characteristics.dtype: uint32 and uint64 (unsigned size arguments np.uint32 and np.uint64); reference signed types np.int32 and np.int64
category_specific_evidence: Negating an unsigned integer underflows and produces a large positive repeats value, per the commit message.
Original code computed repeats = -(-new_size // a.size) (ceil division); with np.uint32(1) the warning 'overflow encountered in scalar negative' appears before SystemError from concatenate.

Reproducer: np.resize(np.array([[23, 95], [66, 37]]), np.int32(1)) returns [23]; the uint32 variant raises SystemError; the uint64 variant raises OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer.
Fix replaces the negation with repeats = (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size.
Added test test_unsigned_resize asserts np.resize(arr, int32(1)) equals np.resize(arr, uint32(1)) and int64(1) equals uint64(1) for arr = [[23, 95], [66, 37]].
Issue reports affected NumPy 2.x (tested v2.3.0 and v2.2.5).
reproduction_risks: The expected value for the unsigned cases is not stated numerically beyond equality with the signed-type result; the signed result [23] is the only explicit value.
Error text in the issue (SystemError, OverflowError) depends on the NumPy version and platform; the passages do not state a precise magnitude of the underflowed repeats value.
The reproducer lacks a stated tolerance; the test uses exact equality (assert_array_equal).
